summary: WSJ reported Nov 17 (after the research close) that the SEC opened a civil probe into Nvidia's disclosures; TechCrunch relays it and Nvidia gave no statement, so it is unverified and cannot be rated material. Also: the board chair said Nov 17 it will not reinstate Huang (headline only), and Huang is said to agree to testify to the Senate Banking Committee. Huang's resignation is already booked (Nov 12 8-K). No driver row moves.

items.headline: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit (WSJ report, relayed)
items.why: New regulatory item outside the research's triggers (the Megaspeed board investigation is a different item). Single relay of WSJ, no company confirmation; the same page says shares fell more than 10% since Huang left, with no date or price, so that figure is not used. Needs WSJ original or an Nvidia filing before it can be called material; scope and any penalty are unsized.
